learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge on: Linear algebra, geometry, differential geometry, differential and integral calculus, differential and partial differential equations, numerical methods and numerical algorithms.

Possess the ability to design, develop, implement, manage and improve products, systems and processes in different industrial areas, using appropriate analytical, computational or experimental techniques.
Apply acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them by working in multidisciplinary teams.
Communicate knowledge and conclusions, both orally and in writing, to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess learning skills that allow continuous study throughout life for adequate professional development.
Incorporate ICT and Industrial Engineering technologies and tools into their professional activities.
Know and apply knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to know, understand and use the principles of differential and integral calculus in one variable.
Ability to know, understand and use the principles of multidimensional differential calculus.
Ability to know, understand and use the results of numerical series and power series.

syllabus_topics: Riemann Integral and Fundamental Theorem of Infinitesimal Calculus: construction and definition of the Riemann integral. Properties of the definite integral.
Fundamental Theorem of Infinitesimal Calculus. Calculation of definite integrals.
Geometric applications: calculation of plane areas. Rectification of curves. Volumes of bodies of revolution. Calculation of volumes by sections.
Improper integrals: first kind, second kind. Integral of unbounded function in unbounded interval.
Real functions of several variables. Level sets. Limits, continuity, partial derivatives, directional derivatives and differential of a scalar function.
Differentiable vector functions. Chain rule: implicit derivatives.
Numerical Series: Sequences. Summable sequences. Series. General criterion of convergence. Geometric series.
Series of positive terms. Integral criterion. Comparison criterion. Ratio and root criteria for series of positive terms.
Series of arbitrary terms. Absolute convergence. Alternating series. Leibniz criterion.

assessment_methods.method: Other activities (individual/group work, cooperative actions, lab practices, class participation)

assessment_rules: Progressive evaluation (EP) consists of individual and group assignments, cooperative actions, lab practices, and class participation, accounting for a maximum of 10% of the evaluation, plus at least two partial tests making up a minimum of 90%. To pass, the resulting EP grade must be 5 or higher. Students scoring 5 or more in EP who wish to modify their grade can take a global exam on the ordinary call date, with the course grade being that obtained in this exam (must be 5 or higher to pass). Students scoring less than 5 in EP can take a global exam (EF) on the ordinary call date, with the course grade being that obtained in this exam (must be 5 or higher to pass). In the extraordinary call, the final grade will be that of the exam, which must be 5 or higher to pass.
